title: Last Moment Before All Ants Fall Out of a Plank
summary: Consider a plank of length n units with ants moving at 1 unit per second, some to the left and some to the right.
statement: Consider a plank of length n units with ants moving at 1 unit per second, some to the left and some to the right. When ants meet, they reverse direction. An ant falls off the end of the plank at time t. Given n, left, and right arrays, determine the time when the last ant falls off.
constraints: Ants move at unit speed; on collision they reverse direction.
Return the last fall time for left-moving and right-moving starting positions.
reference_solution:
def last_ant_fall_moment(n, left, right):
 return max([0]+left+[n-position for position in right])
hints: Colliding identical-speed ants can be viewed as passing through each other because identities do not affect fall times.
A left-moving ant falls after its position; a right-moving one after n-position.
Take the maximum of all such distances.
The pass-through equivalence preserves the multiset of positions and directions after each collision.
editorial: The pass-through equivalence preserves the multiset of positions and directions after each collision.

tests.explanation: A left-moving ant at four takes four seconds, the maximum.
The right-moving ant at zero takes seven seconds.
